standouts.name: Free bookable security time slots
standouts.why: Guaranteed 15-minute window, bookable 3 days ahead for the whole party, QR code by email and a dedicated signed lane. Turns the passenger's biggest uncertainty into an appointment and smooths demand for the operator.

standouts.name: The flight as the organising object (per-flight pages and personal itinerary)
standouts.why: Clean URL per flight number including codeshares; itinerary shows walking time to gate, security wait, boarding time and alerts; arrivals get a landing-to-exit walking-time prediction; 'my travel day' sets crowd expectations.

standouts.name: Schiphol app with glanceable live surfaces
standouts.why: Since v12.0 (Oct 2025) real-time flight updates on home screen, lock screen and Apple Watch; 4.7-4.9 on Google Play across 42-47K reviews; in-app parking booking.

standouts.name: Public Flight API and developer portal
standouts.why: Versioned OpenAPI 3.0 spec (4.2.0) with production and acceptance environments, release notes and a dated migration guide. Makes the airport the default data source for third parties and enforces data discipline internally.

standouts.name: Privium paid membership
standouts.why: Three tiers (EUR 190 / 235 / 370 a year) plus a EUR 95 trial, sold online, bundling fast border passage, lounges and check-in privileges: recurring ancillary revenue from frequent flyers.

weaknesses: Website published in Dutch and English only for a global transfer hub; text service for deaf callers is Dutch-only (search: https://www.schiphol.nl/en/contact-schiphol/).
No door-to-gate ground transport planner: train, bus and taxi pages hand off to NS and 9292, nothing produces a 'leave by' time (search: https://www.schiphol.nl/en/from-to-schiphol/).

Wayfinding depth is app-first and incomplete: blue dot and itinerary walking times live in the app, no public pier-to-pier walking times, no evidence of step-free routing or AR (search + hypothesis: https://www.schiphol.nl/en/blog/find-your-way-quickly-and-easily-at-schiphol/).

Thin AI and account personalisation: an AI chatbot exists but is not a named, marketed assistant; no saved trips or recommendations evidenced; help relies on human agents over WhatsApp (search + hypothesis: https://www.schiphol.nl/en/privacy-and-cookies/schiphol-chatbot-privacy-statement/).

Fragmented commerce and uneven hygiene: click-and-collect was a limited 2021 pilot of unclear status; parking, Privium and lounges are separate purchases; superseded prices and 2020-2023 blogs remain on official URLs; live app flight data was pulled during a security scare; no accessibility statement located (search: https://www.schiphol.nl/en/privium/kieslidmaatschap/ , https://www.schiphol.nl/en/messages/schiphol-responds-to-global-cyber-threat/).
ideas: 'My Journey' without an install: a flight-number URL that opens the full timeline (leave home, check-in close, security and immigration wait, walk to gate, boarding) with opt-in web push and WhatsApp alerts; Schiphol keeps the richest version in its native app.

A true door-to-gate planner for KLIA combining ERL, bus, e-hailing zones, live parking availability and live security and immigration waits into one 'leave by' recommendation, including the Terminal 1 to Terminal 2 transfer.
Multilingual from day one for live data and the assistant, not just static pages: Bahasa Malaysia, English, Chinese, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Tamil.
Accessible wayfinding on the open web: walking times between any two points with a step-free toggle, rest points and prayer rooms, usable in a browser.
One account, one basket: parking, lounge, fast track, reserve-and-collect and points attached to the saved flight with a single checkout, and a visible 'last updated' stamp on every live figure.

Open data plus a public status page: match the Flight API, add queue-time and facility-status endpoints, and keep a cached read-only flight board available when dynamic services are withdrawn for security reasons.
